sections.h2: How is New Mexico laid out for a home seller?
sections.html:
New Mexico has 33 counties, and nearly everything a seller deals with, from valuation to deed recording, happens at the county level. The 2020 census counted 2,117,522 residents, about 17.5 people per square mile across 121,313 square miles of land, so most of the map is sparsely settled and a handful of counties hold most of the people.

Two county profiles show how different the state's corners are. McKinley County, in the northwest, has over 60 percent of its land in the Navajo Nation and Zuni Reservation areas, according to the state labor department. Eddy County, in the southeast, sits inside what Carlsbad's economic development office calls the Permian Basin activity area, with potash, nuclear storage and oil and gas at the center of its economy.

Those differences change what a seller faces: land status questions in one place, an energy-driven economy in another, and a large metro county with the most sales of all. Our guides below are written with that in mind.

sections.h2: Which New Mexico counties are the largest?
sections.html:
Bernalillo County is far ahead, with 676,444 people in 2020, and no other county has even a third of that. The state legislature's official 2020 census table gives these figures for the ten largest.

sections.h2: Which cities does this directory cover?
sections.html:
The directory has city selling pages for Albuquerque, Las Cruces, Rio Rancho, Santa Fe, Roswell, Farmington, Hobbs, Clovis, Carlsbad and Alamogordo, which are the ten largest incorporated places in the 2020 census table. Clovis, in Curry County, counted 38,567 people.

Property tax guides exist for the cities of Albuquerque and Santa Fe and for nine counties: Bernalillo, Sandoval, San Juan, Doña Ana, Eddy, Socorro, Otero, San Miguel and McKinley. The census table puts Socorro County at 16,595 people and San Miguel County at 27,201, so the set spans a metro county and rural counties alike.

  • Use a city page when you want the local picture and how a sale there works.
  • Use a county page when the question is about the assessor, treasurer, dates or appeals.
  • Use a statewide guide for probate, estate tax, deeds and exemptions, which apply everywhere in New Mexico.

sections.h2: Who runs property tax in New Mexico?
sections.html:
County assessors value property, county treasurers collect the tax, and the state Taxation and Revenue Department's Property Tax Division oversees both. The division says residential and non-residential property taxes are assessed by county assessors and collected by county treasurers with its oversight.

The division has three bureaus. The Appraisal Bureau supports assessors and supplies a member to every county valuation protest board. The State Assessed Property Bureau values railroads, pipelines, utilities, airlines, power plants, mineral property and multi-county construction. The Delinquent Property Tax Bureau collects from owners who are three full years behind. The Property Tax Code is Chapter 7, Articles 35 through 38 of the state statutes.

Two figures show the scale. A September 2024 legislative presentation said 531 centrally assessed properties totaled $32 billion in valuation in 2024, about 17 percent of the statewide tax base. Tax year 2022 collections were about $2.58 billion. The Tax Foundation puts the effective property tax rate at 0.63 percent.

sections.h2: What are the same property tax rules in every New Mexico county?
sections.html:
The rules come from state law and apply in all 33 counties, though each county sets its own office hours and payment portals. The list below is the common core.

  • Valuation date: January 1 of each tax year.
  • Taxable value: one third of assessed value.
  • Residential cap: value cannot rise more than 3 percent a year while ownership stays the same, and the cap does not apply to new improvements, rezoning or a change of ownership.
  • Bills: mailed by November 1. First half due November 10, second half due April 10. Interest begins after December 10 and May 10.
  • Lien: attaches January 1 and ranks as a first lien ahead of other interests.
  • Exemptions: a $2,000 head of family exemption for a resident's primary home, and separate veteran exemptions.
  • Protests: written petition to the county assessor within 30 days of the valuation notice mailing, or by April 1 if later.

The state's calendar also says January 10 of the following year is the last day to file a refund claim in district court. Tangible personal property such as livestock and manufactured homes is exempt from the real property tax, according to the same presentation, and certain oil and gas production equipment pays a separate ad valorem tax.

sections.h2: What happens when New Mexico property tax goes delinquent?
sections.html:
Delinquent real property tax can end in a public auction, but only after three full years. The Delinquent Property Tax Bureau notifies owners by phone, certified mail, site visits, notices on the property and newspaper advertising, and it monitors installment agreements. The law requires an auction in each county each calendar year, and the surplus after taxes, interest and costs goes to the former owner.

Because the lien exists from January 1 without any filing, a sale or inheritance does not erase an old balance. This matters most for inherited houses, tired rentals and out-of-state owners.

sections.h2: Is there a New Mexico estate or inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No. The state estate tax was phased out as of January 1, 2005, and New Mexico imposes no inheritance tax. If a federal Form 706 is required, the estate also files the state return and receives a certificate of no tax due. The federal basic exclusion is $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths.

Our New Mexico estate tax guide goes through basis, income tax on estates and what heirs should check before they sell.

Probate is filed in the probate court of the county where the decedent lived, and it is needed when property is titled in the decedent's name. The court's self-help guide says it is not needed for real estate held in joint tenancy or with a recorded transfer on death deed.

The small-estate affidavit covers estates under $50,000 that include no real property. A surviving spouse can receive a primary residence by affidavit after six months if the assessed value is $500,000 or less and other conditions are met. Probate court filing costs $30, and a case can be opened between 5 days and 3 years after death.

sections.h2: How do deeds, recording and sale prices work?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the county clerk, and an unrecorded deed does not affect title against a later purchaser. That rule, in Section 14-9-3 NMSA 1978, is why every county's clerk matters even for a private sale.

New Mexico is also listed among ten states that do not disclose sale prices to the public, in the Taxation and Revenue Department's 2024 presentation. For a seller that means public records give weaker price evidence than in most states, and a written offer and an independent appraisal count for more.

faqs.q: How many counties does New Mexico have?
faqs.a: Thirty-three. Each has its own assessor, treasurer and clerk, and the state Property Tax Division oversees assessors.

faqs.q: What are New Mexico property tax due dates?
faqs.a: November 10 and April 10. Interest begins after December 10 for the first half and after May 10 for the second half.

faqs.q: How much can a New Mexico home's assessed value rise in one year?
faqs.a: By state law, no more than 3 percent for a residence that has not changed ownership, been improved or been rezoned, using the 103 percent and 106.1 percent formula in Section 7-36-21.2.
No. The state has no inheritance tax, and its estate tax was phased out in 2005.

faqs.q: Which New Mexico county is the largest?
faqs.a: Bernalillo County, with 676,444 people in the 2020 census. Albuquerque is the largest city, at 564,559.

faqs.q: Can a New Mexico house be sold at auction for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, after three full years of delinquency. The state's Delinquent Property Tax Bureau runs the auctions, and any surplus after taxes, interest and costs goes to the former owner.
